claim: On host nativestack-5975wx-20260925 on 2026-09-25, ai-memory 2.4.0 was qualified against the installed 2.3.2 and then switched into production. The release asset ai-memory-linux-x86_64.tar.gz (15,969,555 bytes, sha256 590f75ddaf0f8f1a07b70ba20900de717b89c3f6c46e6e5e0540ade302795076) matched the release .sha256 sidecar, the GitHub API asset digest and the release body before it was extracted into a new tools/ai-memory-2.4.0 prefix (binary sha256 360b9dff30537cc514876eab0c4df0d57b9c8c8bb1c62d4a9240f0264e246344, 'ai-memory 2.4.0'). On restored copies of an online backup of the live store, the 2.3.2 baseline passed 16/16 checks on its second attempt (the first failed only its embedding-status probe) and the 2.4.0 rehearsal passed 19/19: migration V64 -> V66 (66 rows) with quick_check ok, 0 pages missing or changed and 0 observations missing; /healthz 200; GET /mcp 405 with allow: POST; protocol 2024-11-05 with 23 tools named as in 2.3.2; the known page's body sha256 equal to the 2.3.2 read; unchanged allowlist check-capture; both the 2.4.0 and the 2.3.2 hook clients captured into the 2.4.0 server; no pre-migration archive; and 2.3.2 serve on the migrated copy exited 1 with 'memory database schema is newer than this ai-memory build'. An independent verifier reproduced these with its own probe code and agreed. The coordinator then performed the user-approved cutover: the service stopped at 20:43:48Z and quiesced (0 ai-memory processes, 0 database users); the quiescent store read V64 (64 rows), quick_check ok, 36 pages and 77,213 observations; an at-rest cold copy (336 files) fingerprint-matched it; bin/ai-memory was relinked to 2.4.0; the upstream install-hooks --apply changed only the binary path on 8 Claude and 7 Codex commands; the service started at 20:44:37Z and applied V65__page_compacted_marker and V66__auto_improve_claim_attempts; /healthz returned 200 with NRestarts 0; the fingerprint compare V64 -> V66 passed (66 rows, quick_check ok, 36 pages with 0 missing or changed, 0 observations missing, 77,330 after); status --json reported 2.4.0; memory_status returned scope resolved_by explicit; a known page's body was unchanged (sha256 prefix 98eb1dfb4fc6b0f5); and a fresh headless claude -p session at 20:45:10Z produced session-start, pre-tool-use, post-tool-use, stop and session-end observations. A read-only read-back at 20:54:04Z found bin/ai-memory on tools/ai-memory-2.4.0, /healthz 200 and 8 Claude plus 7 Codex hook commands on 2.4.0.
limitations: Pending, user-only: Codex skips changed hooks until they are trusted, so the 7 rewritten Codex ai-memory commands capture nothing until the user reviews and trusts them in Codex /hooks; Codex is usage-limited until 2026-09-30. Real Codex capture and Codex-format hook payloads through 2.4.0 were not observed. The rendered adoption/templates/codex.config.template.toml still carries the trusted_hash entries recorded for the pre-switch commands.

The migration is forward-only: after V65 and V66, 2.3.2 refuses the store with DataSchemaAhead, and 2.4.0 writes no automatic pre-migration archive for a store created by 2.x (snapshot_before_db_migration is gated to the 1.x to 2.0 upgrade). Rollback is the coordinator's private at-rest cold copy, a relink to the retained tools/ai-memory-2.3.2 prefix and the installer's .bak-1790369060 hook files; writes made after the cold copy would be lost from the live store. The rollback was not exercised on production, and `ai-memory restore --force` was not run.

GHSA-9pj6-vhgr-3mwh (CVE-2026-63128, rmcp < 2.0.0 Streamable-HTTP session-table leak), fixed by rmcp 2.2.0 in 2.4.0, was not reachable here: the service runs stateless (no --http-stateful; GET /mcp returns 405 with allow: POST) and the leak is in the stateful create_session path. The upgrade removes the three rmcp advisories from the dependency set; it did not close an exposed path on this host, and no exploit was attempted on either version.

The landscape ledger does not move here: catalogs/landscape/foundation.json keeps the durable-memory winner pin ai-memory 2.3.2 from the sealed 2026-09-22 layer-verdict packets. Host receipts recorded at 2.4.0 do not bind to that winner (scripts/host_receipts.py pin_matches) and stay unbound until a new verdict wave re-records the layer.

Linux x86_64 only: adoption/pins-macos-arm64.json keeps ai-memory 2.3.2 (the macos-aarch64 archive) and is unchanged; nothing here is macOS evidence. The shared Claude settings template now names tools/ai-memory-2.4.0, so a Mac that renders it must point the hook commands at its installed 2.3.2 prefix until a Mac qualifies 2.4.0 itself.

Evidence class: our own integration checks (the locally authored aimem_accept.py driver and the verifier's rerun.py) plus coordinator observations; upstream unit and integration tests were not re-run (no Rust toolchain). The cutover facts are coordinator observations exported as aggregates in cutover.json; the cold copy and fingerprint files stay private and were not read by the writing worker.
Integrity rests on three matching upstream checksum values plus the local download hash: the asset has no artifact attestation (HTTP 404) and the release is not immutable.

At the writing worker's 20:54:04Z read-back, the host's installed-versions.txt ai-memory record still read 'ai-memory 2.3.2' (the mcporter record had been updated), so tools that read that record misreport this host until it is updated.

The qualification's own production before/after compare failed 1 of its 19 checks (results/prod-compare-before-after.json, pass false): claude_settings_unchanged, because ~/.claude/settings.json changed at 19:01:59Z during the qualification window. The writer was not identified, and nothing ties the change to this unit: no scratch ai-memory process existed then, install-hooks was not run, and the file's ai-memory hook lines stayed 8 on 2.3.2. Production hook and config files were otherwise fingerprinted only by hash and hook-path counts.

Not observed: whether Claude Code sessions that were already running reload the rewritten hooks (the capture check used a fresh session), 2.4.0 behaviour over time (decay, access reinforcement, scheduler ticks), web UI behaviour beyond /healthz, and the #792 fix, not in 2.4.0 (released in v2.4.1 at 2026-09-25T21:46:32Z). One host (NativeStack, WSL2); the rehearsal used an online backup that is SQLite-consistent but not proven atomic across db, wiki and config, and its scratch servers ran for seconds.
